conclusion: In unseen granulocyte-depleted peripheral blood mononuclear cells from this individual healthy donor assayed under the paired Multiome protocol, single-cell RNA expression variation is not predicted accurately or reliably in absolute terms from ATAC accessibility alone, as the selected predictor {{selected_plan}} ({{selected_name}}) reaches a modest mean per-gene Pearson correlation of {{selected_true_r}} against binomial-thinned RNA counts. When cross-modal predictability is evaluated relative to technical floors and coarse chromatin cell identity across {{n_genes_in_scope}} in-scope genes, {{n_genes_judgeable}} genes have an RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling above the permutation null on held-out cells, whereas {{n_cannot_judge}} unjudgeable genes fail to clear measurement noise and support no claim in either direction. Among the {{n_genes_judgeable}} judgeable genes, {{selected_plan}} exceeds both the ATAC sequencing-depth baseline ({{depth_r}}) and local gene-activity scores ({{gene_activity_r}}), and predicts a specific subset of {{n_beyond}} genes ({{share_beyond}}) significantly better than the ATAC cluster-mean baseline after false-discovery-rate control, while {{n_not_beyond}} judgeable genes show no statistically significant improvement beyond cluster identity.

Even with statistically significant gains on {{n_beyond}} genes, most predictable cross-modal variation reflects coarse cell-type composition rather than fine within-type state. On held-out cells, the ATAC cluster-mean baseline alone attains a mean per-gene correlation of {{cluster_mean_r}} out of the {{ceiling_r}} RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling, so {{selected_plan}} ({{selected_fraction_of_ceiling}} of the ceiling) adds a small mean correlation gain of {{selected_delta_vs_cluster}} and reaches a mean within-cluster correlation of only {{within_cluster_r}}. Gene-level discovery from development cells also generalised poorly: {{selected_plan}} claimed {{n_claimed}} genes beyond cell identity during development, but only {{replication_rate}} of those claimed genes replicated on the held-out split. Moreover, although the tournament chose {{tournament_champion}} out of {{n_candidates}} candidates, {{selected_plan}} placed at rank {{selected_true_rank}} under unified held-out scoring, trailing {{best_true_plan}} by {{selection_gap}} in mean correlation while the largest set of genes predicted beyond cell identity by any candidate reached {{max_beyond_any_plan}}.

These conclusions apply strictly to unseen granulocyte-depleted peripheral blood mononuclear cells from this healthy donor measured with the same paired Multiome assay. They describe statistical association between global chromatin accessibility and thinned transcript counts within this sample, and establish nothing regarding generalisation to other donors, tissues, disease states, or granulocytes, nor do they demonstrate causal chromatin-to-expression gene regulation.
evidence: To prevent target leakage and smoothing artefacts, predictions for unseen donor cells were evaluated strictly against binomial-thinned log-normalised RNA counts while fitting all feature transformations and clusterings exclusively on training splits. Across {{n_genes_in_scope}} in-scope genes on the held-out split, severe single-cell transcript sparsity restricts the mean split-half RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling to {{ceiling_r}}. Technical covariation with ATAC sequencing depth alone yields a mean per-gene correlation of {{depth_r}}, and local chromatin gene-activity aggregation reaches only {{gene_activity_r}}, whereas assigning each unseen cell the mean expression of its ATAC-derived cluster achieves {{cluster_mean_r}}, confirming that discrete lineage identity accounts for most cross-modal signal.

limits: All observations come from granulocyte-depleted peripheral blood mononuclear cells of a single healthy donor under the same Multiome assay, providing no evidence of generalisation to other donors, tissues, disease states, or granulocytes.

Severe single-cell RNA measurement sparsity caps the mean split-half noise ceiling at {{ceiling_r}} across {{n_genes_in_scope}} in-scope genes and leaves {{n_cannot_judge}} genes completely unjudgeable on held-out cells.

Absolute predictive accuracy at the single-cell level remains low even among the {{n_genes_judgeable}} judgeable genes, with a mean held-out correlation of {{selected_true_r}}, a small mean gain of {{selected_delta_vs_cluster}} over the {{cluster_mean_r}} ATAC cluster-mean baseline, and a mean within-cluster correlation of {{within_cluster_r}}.

Per-gene discovery beyond cell identity showed substantial split-to-split instability, as only {{replication_rate}} of the {{n_claimed}} development-claimed genes replicated on held-out evaluation ({{n_beyond}} confirmed genes overall).

Tournament model selection chose {{selected_plan}} (held-out rank {{selected_true_rank}}) over the top held-out candidate {{best_true_plan}}, forfeiting {{selection_gap}} in mean per-gene correlation and capturing {{n_beyond}} genes beyond cell identity compared with up to {{max_beyond_any_plan}} in the candidate pool.

Predictions from global Latent Semantic Indexing components reflect correlational chromatin-to-RNA covariation dominated by abundant immune lineages rather than cis-regulatory mechanisms or causal transcriptional control.
recommendations: Restrict any downstream use of ATAC-predicted expression within this donor context to the {{n_beyond}} held-out-confirmed genes or apply cross-split stability selection, given that development-only discovery ({{n_claimed}} claimed genes) achieved only a {{replication_rate}} held-out replication rate.

Prioritise gene-adaptive multi-mechanism stacking architectures such as {{best_true_plan}} over global ridge regression alone ({{selected_plan}}) when seeking to maximise gene recovery beyond cell identity, as candidate models closed a {{selection_gap}} correlation gap and expanded confirmed genes up to {{max_beyond_any_plan}}.

Align model-selection criteria directly with paired out-of-fold correlation gains over the {{cluster_mean_r}} ATAC cluster-mean baseline and within-cluster correlation ({{within_cluster_r}}) so that tournament ranking does not over-penalise expressive architectures that improve fine-grained prediction.

Acquire paired Multiome datasets spanning multiple donors and enriched for rare immune populations before testing whether chromatin-based expression predictors generalise beyond donor-specific blood cell composition.
